label: node provisioning
type: the step that turns an initialized-but-standalone Couchbase Server node into a cluster member (a one-node cluster, or a node added to an existing one): setting administrator credentials, services and memory quotas. Distinct from and subsequent to node initialization, which only sets disk paths.
evidence: When the node is subsequently provisioned, these are preserved (unless, as is possible with UI-based provisioning, they are optionally overwritten, and the node is thus re-initialized).
Note that disk-paths cannot be changed after a node has been _provisioned_, and has thus either become a cluster of one node, or has been added to a cluster of other nodes.
If initialization is not explicitly performed, it will occur as part of the eventual provisioning process, and default disk-path values will be applied.
note: The initialize/provision distinction is a genuine ordering constraint with an irreversibility attached (disk paths cannot be changed after provisioning) and it exists nowhere in the reference tree - it is a property of the ADMIN WORKFLOW, not of any object. It also explains an otherwise puzzling fact stated by add-node-and-rebalance.md: adding a node ELIMINATES all its prior provisioning, buckets, services and settings. That is only coherent once provisioning is understood as cluster membership rather than as machine setup.
relates_to_competency_question: What is the difference between initializing a node and provisioning it, and which decisions become irreversible?
